title: Logarithmic and exponential functions
overview: Use natural logarithms and e to solve equations and model real-world growth/decay contexts. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Use laws of logarithms and the inverse relationship between eˣ and ln x.
Solve equations and inequalities with an unknown in an exponent.
Transform y = Axⁿ and y = Abˣ to linear form and identify constants from gradient/intercept.
Interpret exponential growth and decay models in context.

definitions.definition: ln x is logarithm to base e and is defined only for x > 0.
eˣ and ln x undo one another: ln(eˣ)=x and eˡⁿˣ=x for x>0.
A quantity whose rate or repeated proportional change is tied to its current value.
Transforming a non-linear relationship into Y = mX + c so a straight-line graph can be used.

sections.title: Logarithms and exponentials
content: Use ln(ab)=ln a+ln b, ln(a/b)=ln a−ln b and ln(aᵏ)=k ln a. A logarithm argument must be positive. The graphs y=eˣ and y=ln x are reflections in y=x; eˣ>0 for all real x, while ln x has vertical asymptote x=0.
bullets: When taking logs of both sides, first ensure both sides are positive.

examples.label: Key relationship
examples.content: Log laws: ln(ab)=ln a+ln b; ln(a/b)=ln a−ln b; ln(aᵏ)=k ln a

sections.title: Solving equations and inequalities
content: Try writing both sides with a common base. Otherwise isolate the exponential expression and take logarithms. For inequalities, remember that eˣ and ln x are increasing, but a base a with 0<a<1 reverses the inequality when comparing exponents.
bullets: Keep logarithms exact until the final numerical evaluation.
Reject roots that make any log argument non-positive.

sections.title: Linearising power laws
content: For y=Axⁿ, take logs to obtain ln y = n ln x + ln A. A plot of ln y against ln x has gradient n and intercept ln A, so A=eⁱⁿᵗᵉʳᶜᵉᵖᵗ. Units and the choice of transformed axes matter.
bullets: Gradient is the exponent, not the coefficient A.
Back-transform the intercept before reporting A.

sections.title: Linearising exponential laws
content: For y=Abˣ, ln y = x ln b + ln A. A plot of ln y against x has gradient ln b. In continuous growth y=Aeᵏˣ, the gradient is k. A negative k models decay; half-life solves eᵏᵗ=1/2.
bullets: State the transformed variables used on each axis.
Interpret constants using the original model, not only the straight line.

formulas.label: Log laws
formulas.expression: ln(ab)=ln a+ln b; ln(a/b)=ln a−ln b; ln(aᵏ)=k ln a

formulas.label: Power-law linearisation
formulas.expression: y=Axⁿ ⇒ ln y = n ln x + ln A

formulas.label: Exponential linearisation
formulas.expression: y=Abˣ ⇒ ln y = x ln b + ln A

diagram.title: Logarithmic and exponential functions: revision route

examTips: Write the log-domain restriction before solving an equation containing ln.
Label transformed graph axes explicitly, including whether common logs or natural logs were used.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using ln(a+b)=ln a+ln b, which is false.
Reporting ln A instead of A from a graph intercept.
Rounding a logarithmic intermediate value too early.

quickRecall.question: How is y=Axⁿ linearised?
quickRecall.answer: Plot ln y against ln x; the gradient is n and the intercept is ln A.

quickRecall.question: What restriction applies to ln f(x)?
How do you recover A from an intercept c=ln A?
What does k<0 mean in y=Aeᵏᵗ?
quickRecall.answer: The quantity decays exponentially as t increases.
